scene_type: 2D (motion in a plane parallel to the image; but the render has visible perspective, see notes)
time_convention: t = frame / 24; frame = round(t * 24); frame 0 = t 0
units: pixels (x right, y down, full resolution) and seconds; no metric scale guessed

camera.motion: static. Phase correlation of the ceiling strip vs frame 0: |shift| <= 0.66 px in all frames (mostly < 0.3 px; sub-pixel noise from lighting changes)
camera.lighting: a bright light patch on the back wall travels ahead of the robot (wall brightness changes strongly over time); the robot also reflects faintly in the window band. The floor and floor lines are unaffected.

perspective.how: intersection of the two diagonal floor marks (box side lines receding toward the camera)
perspective.note: the camera looks roughly perpendicular to the back wall (vanishing point near the image centre). The robot is close to the camera: parts at different depths move at different pixel rates (45.8 to 54.5 px/frame) and the silhouette outline changes as it crosses the image centre.

objects.name: robot
objects.description: blue tracked drilling robot (blue body and head, red handle/top box, black barrel at the back of the head, conical drill and grey claw at the front/right, black tracks with grey road wheels). The only moving object.
objects.direction: left to right (+x), purely horizontal: feature y constant within 0.6 px
objects.partial_frames: 0-8 (rear cut by left border; frame 0 visible fraction 0.26), 33-48 (front cut by right border; frame 48 only a ~10 px sliver at x>=1909)
objects.reference_point_recommended: origin_est_x/origin_est_y in robot.csv: midpoint of the near-side rear corner and the drill tip (linear model, exact for every frame including off-screen extrapolation); y fixed at the bbox centre 582. The true Blender origin is not visible; for speeds/distances only the horizontal pixel rate matters because motion is purely horizontal.

motion_summary_px.type: uniform (constant velocity); per-frame displacement constant within ~0.1-0.4 px for every rigid feature; no start/stop/acceleration visible
motion_summary_px.pixel_rate_spread_note: spread of 45.8-54.5 px/frame is perspective (depth differences across the robot), not acceleration

size_px.height_note: top = top of the red handle on the head, bottom = bottom of the tracks; constant in all frames (pure horizontal motion)
size_px.length_definition: rear of the tracks (silhouette, row 843) to the drill tip (row 655); the drill tip is the rightmost point, the track rear the leftmost point in all frames
size_px.length_vs_frame_px: grows with x from ~600 (frame 8) to 637 (frame 20) to 690 (frame 32), because of perspective (front face visible left of centre, back face right of centre). Column length_px in robot.csv.

sub_parts_at_frame_20.road wheels: 5 visible on the near side, centres at y ~846, spacing ~95 px (wheel hub template repeats every ~95 px; wheels rotate)

events.event: robot already moving at frame 0 (front visible, rear off-screen)
robot rear crosses the left image border (fully in frame)
events.note: fractional frame from the rear-edge fit

events.event: robot centre (origin_est) at image centre x=960
rear silhouette switches from near-side to far-side corner (passes image centre)
drill tip reaches the right image border
last frame with any robot pixels (~10 px sliver)
no start, stop, bounce, contact or direction change; constant velocity throughout
